title: Dear Lord Accept a Sinful Heart
description: Dear Lord Accept a Sinful Heart in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 26, “Self-acquaintance”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear Lord ac-cept a sin-ful heart, Which of it-self com-plains And mourns, with much and fre-quent smart, The e-vil it con-tains.

lines: Dear Lord accept a sinful heart,
Which of itself complains
And mourns, with much and frequent smart,
The evil it contains.
There fiery seeds of anger lurk,
Which often hurt my frame;
And wait but for the tempter's work,
To fan them to a flame.
Legality holds out a bribe
To purchase life from thee;
And discontent would fain prescribe
How thou shalt deal with me.
While unbelief withstands thy grace;
And puts the mercy by;
Presumption, with a brow of brass,
Says, "Give me, or I die."
How eager are my thoughts to roam
In quest of what they love!
But ah! when duty calls them home,
How heavily they move!
O, cleanse me in a Savior's blood,
Transform me by thy pow'r,
And make me thy beloved abode,
And let me rove no more.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
